messages:
maya: Heads up — after the 1.28 rollout in eu-west-1 the GPU nodepools are not scaling. cluster-autoscaler logs spitting errors, pods pending for hours. Anyone seen this?

raj: seeing it. CA logs show it can't map instance IDs to our nodegroups: "no matching node group for instance 'i-0abcd...'". Looks like providerID normalization changed in kubelet.

kevin: same here. We upgraded kubelet + control plane yesterday evening. CA version is 1.28.0, cloudprovider shim expects old providerID format with region prefix.

lucy: Confirmed on one of the stuck jobs: pending because the scale-up doesn't kick off. GPU pools (gpu-reserve-eu) have capacityLocked=false but CA refuses to call Create.

maya: Log snippet from CA: ```E0907 03:12:11.234567 main.go:123] Failed to find node group for instance: i-0abcd1234, providerID: aws:////i-0abcd1234, error: no node group found
```

raj: That providerID pattern `aws:///<id>` is the new normalized shape. Our autoscaler discovery code expects `aws:///eu-west-1/i-...` (region in there). Regression appears after kubelet started normalizing providerID.

kevin: Workarounds: 1) revert kubelet change (not great), 2) patch our CA discovery to accept normalized IDs (preferred), 3) temporary manual scale on ASG.

lucy: We need an emergency mitigation because batch jobs are piling and SLA for training jobs will slip. Manual scale will cost $$ but at least jobs run. Thoughts?

maya: I'm +1 for patching CA discovery today and then rolling the fixed CA image to eu-west-1. I opened a PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/3421 — it maps normalized providerIDs to nodegroup lookup.

infra-bot: Deploy started for image redwood/cluster-autoscaler:fix-providerid-3421 -> staging (eu-west-1). CI: ✅

sre-bot: Alert: pending_pod_count in gpu-reserve-eu crossed threshold (48) — paging on-call.

raj: After applying the patch in staging, CA recognized nodegroups and started scale-ups. We should do canary to 2 clusters then roll. I'll coordinate with deployments.

kevin: Note for follow-up: audit other regions for kubelet providerID behavior and bump CA on all clusters. Also estimate cost impact for the window where we manually scaled ASGs — will add numbers to the incident doc.

lucy: Created incident doc: https://internal.redwood/ops/incidents/2026-09-07-gpu-autoscaler-providerid — adding timeline and cost calc.

maya: TL;DR: root cause = providerID normalization in kubelet (1.28) -> autoscaler discovery mismatch. Fix = small mapping patch in CA (PR 3421). Rollout plan: canary in eu-west-1-staging -> eu-west-1-prod -> other regions.

kevin: @maya @raj please add a short note to the upgrade playbook so future kube upgrades include CA compatibility check (providerID sniffing test).

maya: Will do. Also scheduling a postmortem runbook entry for GPU pools and a cost reconciliation with finance. :spiral_notepad: 

lucy: thanks all, pushing the prod canary now. :thumbsup:
